title.zh: 卷二百〇六 列傳第九十三: 叛臣
title.raw: 卷二百〇六 列傳第九十三: 叛臣 Volume 206 Biographies 93: Contrary Ministers

sentences.zh: 李璮小字松壽，濰州人，李全子也。

translations.literal: Li Tan, whose childhood name was Songsou, was a man of Weizhou and the son of Li Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tan, styled Songsou, was from Weizhou and was the son of Li Quan.

sentences.zh: 或曰璮本衢州徐氏子，父嘗為揚州司理參軍，全蓋養之為子云。

translations.literal: Some say Tan was originally a son of the Xu clan of Quzhou; his father had once served as judicial administrator of Yangzhou, and Quan had adopted him as a son, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Some accounts hold that he was originally a Xu from Quzhou, whose father had served as judicial administrator in Yangzhou and whom Li Quan adopted as his son.

sentences.zh: 太祖十六年，全叛宋，舉山東州郡歸附，太師、國王孛魯承制拜全山東淮南楚州行省，而以其兄福為副元帥。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Taizu, Quan rebelled against Song, bringing the prefectures and districts of Shandong over in submission; the Grand Tutor and King Pelu, acting by imperial commission, appointed Quan Pacification Commissioner for Shandong, Huainan, and Chuzhou, and made his elder brother Fu vice marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In Taizu's sixteenth year, Li Quan defected from the Song and submitted the Shandong prefectures. The Grand Tutor and King Pelu, exercising imperial authority, appointed him regional commissioner for Shandong, Huainan, and Chuzhou, with his elder brother Fu as deputy marshal.

sentences.zh: 太宗三年，全攻宋揚州，敗死。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taizong, Quan attacked Yangzhou of Song and was defeated and died.
translations.idiomatic: In Taizong's third year, Quan attacked the Song at Yangzhou, was defeated, and died.

sentences.zh: 璮遂襲為益都行省，仍得專制其地。

translations.literal: Tan thereupon succeeded as Pacification Commissioner of Yidu and still obtained sole control over that territory.
translations.idiomatic: Tan then inherited the Yidu commission and continued to rule the territory as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 朝廷數徵兵，輒詭辭不至。

translations.literal: When the court repeatedly summoned troops, he always made deceptive excuses and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court called for troops, he found excuses and did not report.

sentences.zh: 憲宗七年，又調其兵赴行在，璮親詣帝言曰：「益都乃宋航海要津，分軍非便。」

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xianzong, troops were again mobilized to the imperial headquarters; Tan personally went before the emperor and said: "Yidu is a vital route for Song navigation by sea; to divide the army would not be convenient."
translations.idiomatic: In Xianzong's seventh year the court again ordered his forces to the capital. Tan went in person and said, "Yidu is a critical Song maritime choke point; splitting the army would be unwise."

sentences.zh: 帝然之，命璮歸取漣海數州。

translations.literal: The emperor approved, and ordered Tan to return and take several prefectures in Lianhai.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and ordered him to go back and take several prefectures in the Lianhai region.

sentences.zh: 璮遂發兵攻拔漣水相連四城，大張剋捷之功。

translations.literal: Tan then dispatched troops, captured and took four contiguous cities including Lianshui, and greatly trumpeted the merit of his victories.
translations.idiomatic: He marched out, seized four linked cities including Lianshui, and loudly advertised his triumphs.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，世祖即位，加璮江淮大都督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong, when Shizu took the throne, Tan was given the additional title of Grand Commander of the Jianghuai region.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongtong, when Shizu ascended the throne, Tan was made Grand Commander of the Jianghuai region.

sentences.zh: 璮言：「近獲生口，知宋調兵將攻漣水。

translations.literal: Tan reported: "Recently we captured prisoners and learned that Song is mobilizing troops and is about to attack Lianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Tan reported, "We have lately taken prisoners who say the Song are massing troops to attack Lianshui.

sentences.zh: 且諜見許浦、射陽湖舟艦相望，勢欲出膠西，向益都，請繕城塹以備。」

translations.literal: Moreover spies have seen ships at Xupu and Sheyang Lake facing one another in formation, with the intent to come out of Jiaoxi toward Yidu; I request that the walls and moats be repaired for defense."
translations.idiomatic: Spies also report warships massed at Xupu and Sheyang Lake, poised to break out of Jiaoxi toward Yidu. I ask that the walls and ditches be repaired in preparation."

sentences.zh: 詔出金符十、銀符五授璮，以賞將士有功者，且賜銀三百錠，降詔獎諭。

translations.literal: An edict issued ten gold tallies and five silver tallies to Tan to reward officers and soldiers who had merit, and also bestowed three hundred ingots of silver, with an imperial decree of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: The court issued ten gold tallies and five silver tallies for Tan to reward meritorious troops, granted three hundred ingots of silver, and sent a commendatory edict.

sentences.zh: 蒙古、漢軍之在邊者，咸聽節制。

translations.literal: Mongol and Han troops on the frontier were all placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: All Mongol and Han forces on the frontier were placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 璮復揚言：「宋呂文德合淮南兵七萬五千，來攻漣水，且規築堡以臨我。

translations.literal: Tan again spread word: "Song's Lü Wende has combined seventy-five thousand Huainan troops to attack Lianshui, and moreover plans to build forts to press upon us.
translations.idiomatic: Tan again spread word: "Song's Lü Wende has combined seventy-five thousand Huainan troops to attack Lianshui and moreover plans to build forts to press upon us.

sentences.zh: 及得賈似道、呂文德書，辭甚悖傲。

translations.literal: When letters from Jia Sidao and Lü Wende were obtained, the wording was extremely insolent and arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Letters from Jia Sidao and Lü Wende that he obtained were brazenly insulting.

sentences.zh: 知朝廷近有內顧之憂，必將肆志於我。

translations.literal: Knowing that the court lately has worries looking inward, they will surely vent their designs upon us.
translations.idiomatic: They know the court has lately been preoccupied with internal troubles and will surely turn on us in earnest.

sentences.zh: 乞選將益兵，臣當帥先渡淮，以雪慢書之辱。」

translations.literal: I beg that generals be selected and troops increased; your subject will lead the vanguard across the Huai to wipe away the shame of these contemptuous letters."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that you choose commanders and reinforce the army; I will lead the crossing of the Huai myself to avenge this insult."

sentences.zh: 執政得奏，諭以「朝廷方通和議，邊將惟當固封圉。

translations.literal: When the chief ministers received the memorial, they instructed him: "The court is presently pursuing peace talks; frontier commanders should only secure the borders.
translations.idiomatic: When the chief ministers received the memorial, they instructed him: "The court is presently pursuing peace talks; frontier commanders should only secure the borders.

sentences.zh: 且南人用間，其詐非一，彼既不至，毋或妄動」。

translations.literal: Moreover the southerners employ stratagems; their deceptions are not of one kind. Since they have not yet come, do not act rashly."
translations.idiomatic: The southerners are skilled in deception; if they have not yet attacked, do not stir rashly."

sentences.zh: 璮乃上言：「臣所領益都，土曠人稀，自立海州，今八載，將士未嘗釋甲，轉輓未嘗息肩，民力凋耗，莫甚斯時，以一路之兵，抗一敵國，衆寡不侔，人所共患。

translations.literal: Tan then submitted a memorial: "The Yidu region I command has broad land and sparse population; since establishing Haizhou, it is now eight years. Officers and soldiers have never laid aside armor, transport and supply have never ceased, and the people's strength is exhausted—never more than at this time. With the troops of one circuit to resist one enemy state, few and many do not match; this is a worry shared by all.
translations.idiomatic: Tan then memorialized: "The Yidu circuit I hold is thinly peopled. For eight years since we took Haizhou my men have never doffed their armor and the transport trains have never stopped; the people are exhausted as never before. One circuit's army against an entire enemy state is a hopeless mismatch, as everyone knows.

sentences.zh: 賴陛下神武，既克漣、海二州，復破夏貴、孫虎臣十餘萬之師。

translations.literal: Relying on Your Majesty's divine martial prowess, we have already taken the two prefectures of Lian and Hai, and again defeated the armies of Xia Gui and Sun Huchen numbering more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to Your Majesty's prowess we have taken Lian and Hai and routed Xia Gui and Sun Huchen's force of more than a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 然臣豈敢恃此必敵人之不再至哉！

translations.literal: Yet how would your subject dare rely on this that the enemy will certainly not come again!
translations.idiomatic: Yet how dare I assume the enemy will not return!

sentences.zh: 且宋人今日西無掣肘，宜得并力而東。

translations.literal: Moreover the Song today have no restraint in the west and ought to be able to combine their strength and advance east.
translations.idiomatic: The Song are no longer tied down in the west and can now concentrate and strike eastward.

sentences.zh: 若以水陸綴漣，而遣舟師遵海以北，擣膠、萊之虛，然後帥步騎直指沂、莒、滕、嶧，則山東非我有矣，豈可易視而不為備哉。

translations.literal: If they link land and water forces at Lian and send a fleet along the sea northward to strike the undefended parts of Jiao and Lai, then lead infantry and cavalry straight at Yi, Ju, Teng, and Yi, then Shandong will no longer be ours—how can this be lightly regarded and not prepared against?
translations.idiomatic: If they pin us at Lian by land and sea, send a fleet north along the coast to raid undefended Jiao and Lai, then march infantry and cavalry on Yi, Ju, Teng, and Yi, Shandong will be lost. How can we treat that lightly or fail to prepare?

sentences.zh: 臣昨追敵至淮安，非不能乘勝取揚、楚，徒以執政止臣，故臣不敢深入。

translations.literal: Your subject yesterday pursued the enemy to Huai'an; it was not that he could not take advantage of victory to seize Yang and Chu, but only because the chief ministers stopped your subject, so he did not dare go deep.
translations.idiomatic: When I pursued the enemy to Huai'an I could have pressed on to Yang and Chu, but the chief ministers held me back, so I did not dare advance further.

sentences.zh: 若以棗陽、唐、鄧、陳、蔡諸軍攻荊山，取壽、泗，以亳、宿、徐、邳諸軍，合臣所統兵，攻揚、楚，則兩淮可定。

translations.literal: If the armies of Zaoyang, Tang, Deng, Chen, and Cai attack Jingshan and take Shou and Si, and the armies of Bo, Su, Xu, and Pi combine with the troops your subject commands to attack Yang and Chu, then the two Huai can be settled.
translations.idiomatic: If the Zaoyang, Tang, Deng, Chen, and Cai armies strike Jingshan and take Shou and Si, while the Bo, Su, Xu, and Pi armies join my command to attack Yang and Chu, both Huai regions can be secured.

sentences.zh: 兩淮既定，則選兵以取江南，自守以寬民力，將無施不可，此上策也。」

translations.literal: Once the two Huai are settled, then select troops to take Jiangnan, hold defensively to ease the people's strength, and generals will have nothing they cannot deploy—this is the superior strategy."
translations.idiomatic: Once the two Huai are secure, chosen troops can take Jiangnan while we hold our ground and spare the people; then every military move will succeed. That is the best plan."

sentences.zh: 因上將校馮泰等功第狀，詔以益都官銀分賞之。

translations.literal: He thereupon submitted a register of merit ranks for officers such as Feng Tai, and an edict ordered that official silver of Yidu be distributed to reward them.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a merit roll for officers such as Feng Tai, and the court ordered Yidu official silver distributed as rewards.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，璮言于行中書省，以宋人聚兵糧數十萬，列艦萬三千艘于許浦，以侵內郡，而宣撫司轉輸不繼，恐一旦水陸道絕，緩急莫報。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, Tan reported to the Branch Secretariat that the Song had gathered several hundred thousand troops and provisions and arrayed thirteen thousand ships at Xupu to invade inner commanderies, while the Pacification Commission's transport and supply did not keep up; he feared that once land and water routes were cut, urgent matters could not be reported.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year Tan told the Branch Secretariat that the Song had massed hundreds of thousands of troops and rations and lined up thirteen thousand ships at Xupu to raid inner districts, while Pacification Commission supply lines were failing; he feared that if land and sea routes were cut he could not report emergencies.

sentences.zh: 請選精騎，倍道來援，表裏協攻，乘機深入，江淮可圖也。

translations.literal: I request that picked cavalry be selected and come by forced marches to reinforce; attack in concert from within and without, seize the opportunity to go deep, and the Jianghuai can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: I ask for picked cavalry sent at forced march to reinforce us, so we can strike together from within and without, press deep while the chance lasts, and take the Jianghuai.

sentences.zh: 既而來獻漣水捷，詔復獎諭，仍給金符十七、銀符二十九，增賜將士。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he came to present news of victory at Lianshui; an edict again commended him, and still issued seventeen gold tallies and twenty-nine silver tallies, with added rewards for officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He soon reported victory at Lianshui; the court commended him again and issued seventeen gold tallies and twenty-nine silver tallies with added rewards for the troops.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，璮輒發兵修益都城塹，且報宋人來攻漣水，詔遣阿朮、哈剌拔都、愛仙不花等悉兵赴之，仍諭度宜益兵赴調。

translations.literal: On gengyin day, Tan on his own authority dispatched troops to repair the walls and moats of Yidu, and also reported that Song troops were coming to attack Lianshui; an edict sent Azhu, Harabatu, and Aixianbuhua and others with all their troops to go there, and still instructed Du Yi to increase troops sent to the mobilization as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengyin day Tan mobilized on his own to repair Yidu's walls and reported a Song attack on Lianshui. The court sent Azhu, Harabatu, Aixianbuhua, and others with full forces and told Du Yi to reinforce the mobilization as needed.

sentences.zh: 璮遂請節制諸道所集兵馬，且請給兵器，中書議與矢三萬，詔給矢十萬。

translations.literal: Tan then requested command over troops gathered from all circuits and also requested arms; the Secretariat deliberated giving thirty thousand arrows, and an edict gave one hundred thousand arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Tan then asked to command troops gathered from all circuits and for weapons; the Secretariat proposed thirty thousand arrows, but the edict granted one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，又以宋賈似道誘緫管張元、張進等書來上。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year, he again presented letters from Song's Jia Sidao enticing the commanders-in-chief Zhang Yuan, Zhang Jin, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year he again submitted letters from the Song minister Jia Sidao trying to win over commanders-in-chief Zhang Yuan, Zhang Jin, and others.

sentences.zh: 蓋璮專制山東者三十餘年，其前後所奏凡數十事，皆恫疑虛喝，挾敵國以要朝廷，而自為完繕益兵計，其謀亦深矣。

translations.literal: For Tan had held sole control of Shandong for more than thirty years; the several dozen matters he memorialized before and after were all intimidation, suspicion, and empty bluster, using the enemy state to demand things of the court while making his own plans to complete fortifications and increase troops—his scheming was also deep.
translations.idiomatic: Tan had ruled Shandong autonomously for more than thirty years. Dozens of memorials he sent were bluffs and threats, using the Song to extort the court while he fortified and armed himself—his designs ran deep.

sentences.zh: 初以其子彥簡質于朝，而潛為私驛，自益都至京師質子營。

translations.literal: At first he sent his son Yanjian as hostage at court, but secretly established a private courier route from Yidu to the hostage camp in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He had earlier sent his son Yanjian to court as a hostage, but secretly maintained a private courier line from Yidu to the hostage quarters in the capital.

sentences.zh: 至是，彥簡遂用私驛逃歸。

translations.literal: At this time Yanjian then used the private courier route to flee and return.
translations.idiomatic: Now Yanjian used that private route to escape home.

sentences.zh: 璮遂反，以漣、海三城獻于宋，殲蒙古戍兵，引麾下具舟艦，還攻益都。

translations.literal: Tan then rebelled, presented the three cities of Lian and Hai to Song, annihilated Mongol garrison troops, led his followers with ships fully equipped, and returned to attack Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Tan then rebelled, surrendered the three Lian-Hai cities to the Song, wiped out the Mongol garrisons, and led his fleet back to attack Yidu.

sentences.zh: 甲午，入之，發府庫以犒其黨，遂寇蒲臺。

translations.literal: On jiawu day he entered it, opened the government treasuries to reward his faction, and then raided Putai.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu day he entered the city, opened the treasuries to reward his followers, and raided Putai.

sentences.zh: 民聞璮反，皆入保城郭，或奔竄山谷，由是自益都至臨淄數百里，寂無人聲。

translations.literal: When the people heard Tan had rebelled, they all entered walled towns for protection or fled scattering into valleys and mountains; from this, from Yidu to Linzi for several hundred li, there was silence and no human sound.
translations.idiomatic: When the people heard of the rebellion they fled into walled towns or scattered into the hills, and for several hundred li from Yidu to Linzi the countryside fell silent.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，帝聞璮反，遂下詔暴其罪。

translations.literal: On guimao day the emperor heard Tan had rebelled and thereupon issued an edict exposing his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao day the emperor learned of the rebellion and issued an edict listing Tan's crimes.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，命諸軍討璮。

translations.literal: On jiachen day he ordered all armies to suppress Tan.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiachen day he ordered all armies to suppress Tan.

sentences.zh: 己酉，以璮故，戮中書平章王文統。

translations.literal: On jiyou day, on account of Tan, the Secretariat Grand Councillor Wang Wentong was executed.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiyou day, because of Tan's rebellion, Grand Councillor Wang Wentong of the Secretariat was executed.

sentences.zh: 壬子，璮盜據濟南。

translations.literal: On renzi day Tan seized and occupied Jinan by force.
translations.idiomatic: On the renzi day Tan seized Jinan.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，命史樞、阿朮帥師赴濟南。

translations.literal: On guiyou day Shi Shu and Azhu were ordered to lead armies to Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou day Shi Shu and Azhu were ordered to march on Jinan.

sentences.zh: 璮帥衆出掠輜重，將及城，官軍邀擊，大敗之，斬首四千級，璮退保濟南。

translations.literal: Tan led his masses out to plunder baggage trains; when he was about to reach the city, government troops intercepted and attacked, inflicting a great defeat, beheading four thousand, and Tan withdrew to hold Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Tan led his men out to raid supply trains near the city; government troops intercepted him, inflicted a crushing defeat with four thousand heads taken, and Tan fell back to defend Jinan.

sentences.zh: 五月庚申，築環城圍之；

translations.literal: In the fifth month on gengshen day, a encircling wall was built to besiege it;
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day of the fifth month they built a ring wall to besiege the city;

sentences.zh: 甲戌，圍合。

translations.literal: On jiaxu day the encirclement closed.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu day the encirclement closed.

sentences.zh: 璮自是不得復出，猶日夜拒守，取城中子女賞將士，以悅其心；

translations.literal: From this Tan could not come out again; he still resisted day and night, took the sons and daughters within the city to reward officers and soldiers and please their hearts;
translations.idiomatic: Tan could no longer break out but still held day and night, giving the city's sons and daughters to his officers as rewards to keep their loyalty;

sentences.zh: 且分軍就食民家，發其蓋藏以繼，不足，則家賦之鹽，令以人為食。

translations.literal: Moreover he divided troops to take food from civilian households, opened their stored goods to continue supply, and when insufficient, levied salt per household and ordered that people be used as food.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent troops to live off civilian households, seized hidden stores to keep supplies going, and when that failed levied salt per household and ordered cannibalism.

sentences.zh: 至是，人情潰散，璮不能制，各什伯相結，縋城以出。

translations.literal: By this time morale collapsed and Tan could not control it; men formed groups of tens and hundreds, lowered themselves from the wall by rope, and went out.
translations.idiomatic: By then morale collapsed beyond Tan's control; men banded in tens and hundreds and lowered themselves from the walls to escape.

sentences.zh: 璮知城且破，乃手刃愛妾，乘舟入大明湖，自投水中，水淺不得死，為官軍所獲，縛至諸王合必赤帳前。

translations.literal: Tan knew the city was about to fall; he then personally killed his beloved concubine, boarded a boat into Daming Lake, and threw himself into the water; the water was shallow and he did not die, was captured by government troops, bound, and brought before the tent of Prince Qubilai.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the city would fall, Tan killed his favorite concubine with his own hand, took a boat onto Daming Lake, and threw himself into the water; the lake was shallow and he survived, was captured, bound, and brought before Prince Qubilai's tent.

sentences.zh: 丞相史天澤言：「宜即誅之，以安人心。」

translations.literal: Chancellor Shi Tianze said: "He should be executed at once to settle people's hearts."
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Shi Tianze said, "He should be executed at once to reassure the people."

sentences.zh: 遂與蒙古軍官囊家并誅焉。

translations.literal: He was then executed together with the Mongol officer Nangia.
translations.idiomatic: He was then executed together with the Mongol officer Nangia.

sentences.zh: 王文統字以道，益都人也。

translations.literal: Wang Wentong, styled Yidao, was a man of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wentong, styled Yidao, was from Yidu.

sentences.zh: 少時讀權謀書，好以言撼人。

translations.literal: In youth he read books of stratagem and power, and liked to sway people with words.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied works of strategy and loved to sway people with his rhetoric.

sentences.zh: 遍干諸侯，無所遇，乃往見李璮。

translations.literal: He went about presenting himself to all the lords and met with nothing; he then went to see Li Tan.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned lords everywhere without success, then went to see Li Tan.

sentences.zh: 璮與語，大喜，即留置幕府，命其子彥簡師事之，文統亦以女妻璮。

translations.literal: Tan conversed with him and was greatly pleased, immediately kept him in the headquarters, ordered his son Yanjian to take him as teacher, and Wentong also gave his daughter in marriage to Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Tan was delighted at their talk, kept him in his headquarters, had his son Yanjian study under him, and Wentong gave his daughter to Tan in marriage.

sentences.zh: 由是軍旅之事，咸與諮決，歲上邊功，虛張敵勢，以固其位，用官物樹私恩，取宋漣、海二郡，皆文統謀也。

translations.literal: From this all military affairs were consulted and decided with him; each year he reported frontier merit, inflated enemy strength to secure his position, used official goods to build private favor, and the taking of the two Song prefectures Lian and Hai were all Wentong's schemes.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter all military matters went through him; each year he reported frontier victories, inflated enemy threats to secure his position, used public goods to buy private loyalty, and the capture of the Song prefectures Lian and Hai was his doing.

sentences.zh: 世祖在潛藩，訪問才智之士，素聞其名。

translations.literal: When Shizu was in his princely establishment, he sought out men of talent and wisdom and had long heard his name.
translations.idiomatic: While Shizu was still heir apparent he sought men of talent and had long heard of Wentong.

sentences.zh: 及即位，厲精求治，有以文統為薦者，亟召用之。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, he applied himself diligently to good government; when someone recommended Wentong, he quickly summoned and employed him.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne and threw himself into reform, someone recommended Wentong and he was summoned at once.

sentences.zh: 乃立中書省，以緫內外百司之政，首擢文統為平章政事，委以更張庶務。

translations.literal: He then established the Secretariat to oversee the government of all inner and outer offices; Wentong was first promoted to Grand Councillor and entrusted with reforming all routine affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He established the Secretariat to govern all departments, made Wentong its first Grand Councillor, and charged him with overhauling administration.

sentences.zh: 建元為中統，詔諭天下，立十路宣撫司，示以條格，欲差發辦而民不擾，鹽課不失常額，交鈔無致阻滯。

translations.literal: The era name was established as Zhongtong; an edict announced this to all under Heaven, ten-circuit Pacification Commissions were established, regulations were displayed, with the aim that corvée assignments be carried out yet the people not be disturbed, salt levies not fall below the regular quota, and paper notes not meet obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: The era was named Zhongtong; edicts went out to establish Pacification Commissions in ten circuits with regulations so corvée could be met without harassing the people, salt revenues kept steady, and paper currency kept flowing.

sentences.zh: 尋詔行中書省造中統元寶交鈔，立互市于潁州、漣水、光化軍。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward an edict ordered the Branch Secretariat to mint Zhongtong yuanbao paper notes and establish mutual markets at Yingzhou, Lianshui, and Guanghua Army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Branch Secretariat was ordered to issue Zhongtong treasure notes and open trade markets at Yingzhou, Lianshui, and Guanghua Army.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，初行中統交鈔，自十文至二貫文，凡十等，不限年月，諸路通行，稅賦並聽收受。

translations.literal: That winter the Zhongtong notes were first put in circulation, from ten cash to two strings, ten denominations in all, with no limit on year or month, circulating in all circuits, and taxes and levies were all permitted to be received in them.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Zhongtong notes were first issued in ten denominations from ten cash to two strings, valid everywhere without expiry, and accepted for taxes.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，世祖在開平，召行中書省事禡禡與文統，親率各路宣撫使俱赴闕。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year Shizu was at Kaiping; he summoned the Branch Secretariat chief Mamma and Wentong, and personally led the Pacification Commissioners of all circuits together to the court.
translations.idiomatic: The following second month, while Shizu was at Kaiping, he summoned Branch Secretariat chief Mamma and Wentong and had all circuit Pacification Commissioners come to court with him.

sentences.zh: 世祖自去秋親征叛王阿里不哥于北方，凡民間差發、宣課鹽鐵等事，一委文統等裁處。

translations.literal: Since the previous autumn Shizu had personally campaigned against the rebel prince Ariq Böke in the north; all matters of civilian corvée, salt and iron levies, and the like were entirely entrusted to Wentong and others to decide.
translations.idiomatic: Since the previous autumn Shizu had been campaigning north against the rebel prince Ariq Böke; all corvée, salt, iron, and related levies were left entirely to Wentong and his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 及振旅還宮，未知其可否何若，且以往者，急於用兵，事多不暇講究，所當振其紀綱者，宜在今日。

translations.literal: When the army returned in triumph to the palace, it was not known how effective these had been; moreover in the past, urgent with military use, many matters had no leisure for thorough study—what should restore discipline ought to be done today.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned he did not yet know how well these measures had worked; wartime urgency had left much undone, and the time to restore discipline was now.

sentences.zh: 故召文統等至，責以成效，用游顯、鄭鼎、趙良弼、董文炳等為各路宣撫司，復以所議條格詔諭各路，俾遵行之。

translations.literal: Therefore Wentong and others were summoned and charged with results; You Xian, Zheng Ding, Zhao Liangbi, Dong Wenbing, and others were appointed to Pacification Commissions of the circuits, and again the regulations they had deliberated were proclaimed to all circuits to be obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore summoned Wentong and demanded results, appointed You Xian, Zheng Ding, Zhao Liangbi, Dong Wenbing, and others as circuit Pacification Commissioners, and reissued the regulations for all circuits to follow.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又詔諭宣撫司，并達魯花赤管民官、課稅所官，申嚴私鹽、酒醋、麯貨等禁。

translations.literal: Before long, another edict instructed the Pacification Commissions, together with darughachi, civilian officials, and tax-office officials, to strictly enforce prohibitions on private salt, wine, vinegar, yeast goods, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Soon another edict told Pacification Commissions, darughachi, civilian officials, and tax officers to enforce bans on private salt, liquor, vinegar, and yeast products.

sentences.zh: 文統為人忌刻，初立中書時，張文謙為左丞。

translations.literal: Wentong was jealous and harsh by nature; when the Secretariat was first established, Zhang Wenqian was Left Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Wentong was jealous by nature; when the Secretariat was first set up Zhang Wenqian was Left Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 文謙素以安國利民自負，故凡講論建明，輒相可否，文統積不能平，思有以陷之，文謙竟以本職行大名等路宣撫司事而去。

translations.literal: Wenqian had always prided himself on securing the state and benefiting the people; therefore whenever policies were discussed and proposed, they constantly opposed each other. Wentong's resentment could not be settled and he sought means to trap him; Wenqian in the end left to carry out Pacification Commission affairs for Daming and other circuits in his original post.
translations.idiomatic: Wenqian prided himself on serving state and people and constantly disputed Wentong's proposals; Wentong brooded until he found a way to remove him, and Wenqian was sent off to handle Pacification affairs in Daming and other circuits.

sentences.zh: 時姚樞、竇默、許衡，皆世祖所敬信者，文統諷世祖授樞為太子太師，默為太子太傅，衡為太子太保，外佯尊之，實不欲使朝夕備顧問於左右也。

translations.literal: At that time Yao Shu, Dou Mo, and Xu Heng were all men Shizu respected and trusted; Wentong urged Shizu to appoint Shu as Grand Tutor of the Heir, Mo as Grand Mentor of the Heir, and Heng as Grand Guardian of the Heir—outwardly feigning honor while in fact not wishing them to attend day and night as advisers at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shu, Dou Mo, and Xu Heng were men Shizu trusted; Wentong had him appoint them Grand Tutor, Grand Mentor, and Grand Guardian of the Heir—honors in name meant to keep them from daily counsel at court.

sentences.zh: 默嘗與王鶚及樞、衡俱侍世祖，面詆文統曰：「此人學術不正，必禍天下，不可處以相位。」

translations.literal: Mo once attended Shizu together with Wang E and Shu and Heng, and to his face denounced Wentong, saying: "This man's learning is not correct; he will surely bring calamity on all under Heaven and must not be placed in the chancellorship."
translations.idiomatic: Mo once attended Shizu with Wang E, Yao Shu, and Xu Heng and denounced Wentong to his face: "This man's learning is unsound; he will ruin the realm and must not hold the chancellorship."

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「若是，則誰可為者？」

translations.literal: Shizu said: "If so, then who can do it?"
translations.idiomatic: Shizu asked, "If so, who can?"

sentences.zh: 默以許衡對，世祖不懌而罷。

translations.literal: Mo answered with Xu Heng; Shizu was displeased and dismissed the session.
translations.idiomatic: Mo named Xu Heng; Shizu was displeased and ended the audience.

sentences.zh: 鶚嘗請以右丞相史天澤監修國史，左丞相耶律鑄監修遼史，文統監修金史。

translations.literal: E once requested that Right Chancellor Shi Tianze supervise compilation of the national history, Left Chancellor Yelü Zhu supervise compilation of the Liao history, and Wentong supervise compilation of the Jin history.
translations.idiomatic: Wang E once proposed that Right Chancellor Shi Tianze supervise the dynastic history, Left Chancellor Yelü Zhu the Liao history, and Wentong the Jin history.

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「監修階銜，俟修史時定之。」

translations.literal: Shizu said: "The supervisory rank and title will be fixed when the histories are compiled."
translations.idiomatic: Shizu replied, "Supervisory titles will be fixed when the histories are actually compiled."

sentences.zh: 又明年二月，李璮反，以漣、海三城獻于宋。

translations.literal: In the second month of the year after next, Li Tan rebelled and presented the three cities of Lian and Hai to Song.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year Li Tan rebelled and surrendered the three Lian-Hai cities to the Song.

sentences.zh: 先是，其子彥簡，由京師逃歸，璮遣人白之中書。

translations.literal: Earlier, his son Yanjian had fled from the capital and returned; Tan sent a man to report this to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier his son Yanjian had escaped from the capital; Tan sent word to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及反書聞，人多言文統嘗遣子蕘與璮通音耗。

translations.literal: When news of the rebellion was heard, many said Wentong had once sent his son Rao to exchange messages with Tan.
translations.idiomatic: When news of the rebellion arrived, many said Wentong had sent his son Rao to exchange messages with Tan.

sentences.zh: 世祖召文統問之曰：「汝教璮為逆，積有歲年，舉世皆知之。

translations.literal: Shizu summoned Wentong and questioned him, saying: "You taught Tan to rebel; this has accumulated for years and the whole world knows it.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu summoned Wentong and said, "You taught Tan to rebel; everyone has known it for years.

sentences.zh: 朕今問汝所策云何，其悉以對。」

translations.literal: I now ask what your stratagems were—report them all fully."
translations.idiomatic: I ask what your plans were—tell me everything."

sentences.zh: 文統對曰：「臣亦忘之，容臣悉書以上。」

translations.literal: Wentong answered: "Your subject has also forgotten; allow your subject to write it all out and submit it above."
translations.idiomatic: Wentong replied, "I have forgotten; let me write it all out and submit it."

sentences.zh: 書畢，世祖命讀之，其間有曰：「螻蟻之命，苟能存全，保為陛下取江南。」

translations.literal: When the writing was finished, Shizu ordered it read aloud; among its passages was: "This ant's life, if it can be preserved whole, I guarantee to take Jiangnan for Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: When he finished writing, Shizu had it read aloud; it included, "If this wretch's life is spared, I guarantee to take Jiangnan for Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「汝今日猶欲緩頰於朕耶？」

translations.literal: Shizu said: "Do you still today wish to plead for your cheeks before me?"
translations.idiomatic: Shizu said, "Do you still think you can talk your way out?"

sentences.zh: 會璮遣人持文統三書自洺水至，以書示之，文統始錯愕駭汗。

translations.literal: Just then Tan sent a man bearing three letters of Wentong from Ming River; when the letters were shown him, Wentong at last was startled and broke into terrified sweat.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Tan's messenger arrived from Ming River with three letters from Wentong; when they were shown him, Wentong turned pale and broke into a sweat.

sentences.zh: 書中有「期甲子」語，世祖曰：「甲子之期云何？」

translations.literal: In the letters was the phrase "appointed on jiazi"; Shizu said: "What is the meaning of the jiazi appointment?"
translations.idiomatic: The letters mentioned a "jiazi appointment"; Shizu asked, "What does the jiazi date mean?"

sentences.zh: 文統對曰：「李璮久蓄反心，以臣居中，不敢即發，臣欲告陛下縛璮久矣，第緣陛下加兵北方，猶未靖也。

translations.literal: Wentong answered: "Li Tan long harbored rebellious intent; because your subject was at the center, he did not dare launch at once. Your subject wished to tell Your Majesty to bind Tan long ago, but only because Your Majesty was adding troops in the north and it was not yet settled.
translations.idiomatic: Wentong answered, "Li Tan long planned rebellion but dared not act while I was at court. I meant to tell Your Majesty to arrest him, but you were still campaigning in the north.

sentences.zh: 比至甲子，猶可數年，臣為是言，姑遲其反期耳。」

translations.literal: By the time jiazi came it would still be several years; your subject made this statement merely to postpone his time of rebellion for a while."
translations.idiomatic: The jiazi day was still years away; I said that only to delay his rebellion."

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「無多言。

translations.literal: Shizu said: "Say no more.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu said, "Enough.

sentences.zh: 朕拔汝布衣，授之政柄，遇汝不薄，何負而為此？」

translations.literal: I raised you from common cloth and gave you the reins of government; I treated you not thinly—what did I fail in that you did this?"
translations.idiomatic: I raised you from the ranks and gave you power; I treated you generously—what grievance made you do this?"

sentences.zh: 文統猶枝辭傍說，終不自言「臣罪當死」，乃命左右斥去，始出就縛。

translations.literal: Wentong still branched into side arguments and in the end did not himself say "your subject's crime deserves death"; he was then ordered dismissed by attendants and only then went out to be bound.
translations.idiomatic: Wentong still hedged and would not say, "Your subject's crime deserves death"; attendants were ordered to remove him, and only then did he go out to be bound.

sentences.zh: 猶召竇默、姚樞、王鶚、僧子聰及張柔等至，示以前書曰：「汝等謂文統當得何罪？」

translations.literal: He still summoned Dou Mo, Yao Shu, Wang E, the monk Zicong, and Zhang Rou and others, showed them the earlier writing, and said: "What crime do you say Wentong deserves?"
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned Dou Mo, Yao Shu, Wang E, the monk Zicong, Zhang Rou, and others, showed them the document, and asked, "What punishment does Wentong deserve?"

sentences.zh: 文臣皆言「人臣無將，將而必誅」。

translations.literal: The civil officials all said: "A minister must not harbor rebellion; if he does, he must be executed."
translations.idiomatic: The civil officials said, "A subject who rebels must die."

sentences.zh: 柔獨疾聲大言曰：「宜剮！」

translations.literal: Rou alone cried out in a loud voice: "He should be dismembered!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rou alone shouted, "He should be dismembered!"

sentences.zh: 世祖又曰：「汝同辭言之。」

translations.literal: Shizu again said: "Speak in the same words."
translations.idiomatic: Shizu said, "Say it together."

sentences.zh: 諸臣皆曰：「當死。」

translations.literal: All the ministers said: "He should die."
translations.idiomatic: All said, "Death."

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「渠亦自服朕前矣。」

translations.literal: Shizu said: "He has also himself submitted before me."
translations.idiomatic: Shizu said, "He has already submitted before me."

sentences.zh: 文統乃伏誅。

translations.literal: Wentong then submitted to execution.
translations.idiomatic: Wentong was then executed.

sentences.zh: 子蕘，并就戮。

translations.literal: His son Rao was also executed together.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rao was executed with him.

sentences.zh: 詔諭天下曰：「人臣無將，垂千古之彝訓；

translations.literal: An edict announced to all under Heaven: "A minister must not harbor rebellion—this is the constant instruction handed down through the ages;
translations.idiomatic: An edict went to the realm: "Rebellion by a minister violates eternal law;

sentences.zh: 國制有定，懷二心者必誅。

translations.literal: the state's regulations are fixed; those who harbor two hearts must be executed.
translations.idiomatic: our dynastic rule is clear: double-dealing means death.

sentences.zh: 何期輔弼之僚，迺蓄姦邪之志。

translations.literal: Who would have expected that among assisting and supporting colleagues, one would harbor treacherous and evil intent.
translations.idiomatic: Who could expect a chief counselor to nurse treachery?

sentences.zh: 平章政事王文統，起由下列，擢置台司，倚付不為不深，待遇不為不厚，庶收成效，以底丕平。

translations.literal: Grand Councillor Wang Wentong, rising from the lower ranks, was raised to the high office; trust placed in him was not shallow, treatment was not thin, hoping to harvest results and bring great peace.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councillor Wang Wentong rose from humble ranks to the highest office; the trust and favor shown him were abundant, in hopes he would bring great peace.

sentences.zh: 焉知李璮之同謀，潛使子蕘之通耗。

translations.literal: Who knew his conspiracy with Li Tan, secretly sending his son Rao to exchange messages.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he conspired with Li Tan and sent his son Rao to pass secret messages.

sentences.zh: 邇者獲親書之數幅，審其有反狀者累年，宜加肆市之誅，以著滔天之惡。

translations.literal: Recently several sheets of his own handwriting were obtained, confirming that his rebellious conduct had accumulated for years; he should receive execution by dismemberment in the market to display his heaven-overflowing evil.
translations.idiomatic: Recent letters in his own hand prove years of treason; he deserves public dismemberment to mark his monstrous crime.

sentences.zh: 已於今月二十三日，將反臣王文統并其子蕘，正典刑訖。

translations.literal: On the twenty-third day of this month, the rebel minister Wang Wentong together with his son Rao have been subjected to proper statutory punishment and it is finished.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-third of this month the rebel Wang Wentong and his son Rao have been duly executed.

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 負國恩而謀大逆，死有餘辜；

translations.literal: Bearing the state's favor yet plotting great rebellion, even death leaves guilt remaining;
translations.idiomatic: Betraying imperial favor to plot rebellion, death still leaves guilt unpaid;

sentences.zh: 處相位而被極刑，時或未喻。

translations.literal: holding the chancellorship yet suffering extreme punishment—the times perhaps did not understand.
translations.idiomatic: a chancellor put to extreme punishment may puzzle the age.

sentences.zh: 咨爾有衆，體予至懷。」

translations.literal: Take counsel, all you multitudes, and embody my utmost heartfelt intent."
translations.idiomatic: Hear this, all my people, and know my deepest mind."

sentences.zh: 然文統雖以反誅，而元之立國，其規模法度，世謂出於文統之功為多云。

translations.literal: Yet although Wentong was executed for rebellion, in the Yuan's establishing the state, its scope and institutions—the world says largely issued from Wentong's merit.
translations.idiomatic: Yet though Wentong died a traitor, posterity largely credits him with shaping the Yuan state's institutions and scope.

sentences.zh: 阿魯輝帖木兒，滅里大王之裔也。

translations.literal: Arugh Temür was a descendant of Great Prince Mieli.
translations.idiomatic: Arugh Temür was a descendant of Great Prince Mieli.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗生七子，而滅里位第七。

translations.literal: At the outset, Taizong had seven sons, and Mieli ranked seventh.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset, Taizong had seven sons, and Mieli ranked seventh.

sentences.zh: 世祖既定天下，乃大封宗親為王，滅里其一也。

translations.literal: After Shizu had settled the realm, he greatly enfeoffed kinsmen as princes, and Mieli was one of them.
translations.idiomatic: After Shizu had settled the realm, he enfeoffed many kinsmen as princes, and Mieli was one of them.

sentences.zh: 滅里生脫忽，脫忽生俺都剌，俺都剌生禿滿，至大元年，始封陽翟王，賜金印螭紐，俾鎮北藩。

translations.literal: Mieli begot Toqhu; Toqhu begot Andula; Andula begot Tuman. In the first year of Zhide, Tuman was first enfeoffed as Prince of Yangdi, granted a gold seal with dragon knob, and charged to guard the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Mieli begot Toqhu; Toqhu begot Andula; Andula begot Tuman. In the first year of Zhide, Tuman was first enfeoffed as Prince of Yangdi, granted a gold seal with dragon knob, and charged to guard the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 禿滿傳曲春，曲春傳太平，太平傳帖木兒赤，而阿魯輝帖木兒襲其封。

translations.literal: Tuman passed the title to Quchun; Quchun to Taiping; Taiping to Temürchi; and Arugh Temür inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Tuman passed the title to Quchun; Quchun to Taiping; Taiping to Temürchi; and Arugh Temür inherited the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 會兵起汝、潁，天下皆震動，帝屢詔宗王，以北方兵南討。

translations.literal: When troops rose in Ru and Ying, all under Heaven was shaken; the emperor repeatedly issued an edict the princes to bring northern troops south to suppress.
translations.idiomatic: When rebellion broke out in Ru and Ying the realm was shaken, and the emperor repeatedly ordered the princes to march southern campaigns with northern troops.

sentences.zh: 阿魯輝帖木兒知國事已不可為，乃乘間擁衆數萬，屯于木兒古兀徹之地，而脅宗王以叛。

translations.literal: Arugh Temür knew the state's affairs could no longer be remedied; he took the interval to gather several tens of thousands, encamped in the land of Mu'er Gu'uji, and coerced princes into rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Arugh Temür saw the dynasty could not be saved, seized the moment to gather tens of thousands at Mu'er Gu'uji, and forced princes into rebellion.

sentences.zh: 且遣使來言於帝曰：「祖宗以天下付汝，汝何故失其太半，盍以國璽授我，我當自為之。」

translations.literal: He also sent envoys to tell the emperor: "The ancestors entrusted all under Heaven to you—why have you lost more than half? Why not give me the imperial seal? I shall act for myself."
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys telling the emperor, "Our forefathers gave you the realm and you have lost more than half of it. Hand me the imperial seal and I will rule myself."

sentences.zh: 帝聞，神色自若，徐曰：「天命有在，汝欲為則為之。」

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, his expression was calm; he said slowly: "Heaven's mandate has its place—if you wish to act, then act."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard this calmly and said slowly, "Heaven's mandate endures; do as you will."

sentences.zh: 於是降詔開諭，俾其悔罪，阿魯輝帖木兒不聽。

translations.literal: He then issued an edict to enlighten and instruct him to repent his crime, but Arugh Temür would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent edicts urging repentance, but Arugh Temür would not heed them.

sentences.zh: 乃命知樞密院事禿堅帖木兒等擊之。

translations.literal: He then ordered the Privy Council director Toqash Temür and others to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Privy Council director Toqash Temür and others to attack him.

sentences.zh: 行至稱海，起哈剌赤萬人為軍。

translations.literal: When the army reached Chinghai, ten thousand Kharchin were raised as troops.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Chinghai, he raised ten thousand Kharchin as an army.

sentences.zh: 其人素不習為兵，而一旦驅之使戰，既陣，兵猶未接，皆脫其號衣，奔阿魯輝帖木兒軍中，禿堅帖木兒軍遂敗績，單騎還上都。

translations.literal: These men were never accustomed to being soldiers, yet were suddenly driven to fight; once the battle lines were formed, before the armies had even engaged, they all stripped off their uniform coats and fled to Arugh Temür's army. Toqash Temür's army was then defeated, and he returned alone on horseback to Shangdu.
translations.idiomatic: They were not trained soldiers and were suddenly sent to battle; before the lines met they stripped their uniforms and defected to Arugh Temür. Toqash Temür's force was routed and he fled alone to Shangdu.

sentences.zh: 至正二十一年，更命少保、知樞密院事老章，以兵十萬擊之，且俾阿魯輝帖木兒之弟忽都帖木兒從征軍中，遂大敗其衆。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Zhizheng, he again ordered Junior Guardian and Privy Council director Lao Zhang, with one hundred thousand troops, to attack him, and moreover had Arugh Temür's younger brother Qutu Temür follow in the campaign army; they then inflicted a great defeat on his masses.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 21 he sent Junior Guardian and Privy Council director Lao Zhang with one hundred thousand men, including Arugh Temür's brother Qutu Temür in the army, and they crushed the rebel force.

sentences.zh: 阿魯輝帖木兒遂謀東遁。

translations.literal: Arugh Temür then planned to flee east.
translations.idiomatic: Arugh Temür then planned to flee eastward.

sentences.zh: 其部將脫驩知其勢窮，乃與宗王囊加、玉樞虎兒吐華擒阿魯輝帖木兒送闕下，帝命誅之。

translations.literal: His officer Toqan, knowing his force was exhausted, then together with Princes Nangia and Yushu Huer Tuhua seized Arugh Temür and sent him to the court; the emperor ordered him executed.
translations.idiomatic: His officer Toqan, seeing defeat was near, joined Princes Nangia and Yushu Huer Tuhua in seizing Arugh Temür and sending him to court, where the emperor ordered his execution.

sentences.zh: 於是加老章太傅，脫驩知遼陽行樞密院事，仍以忽都帖木兒襲封陽翟王，而宗王囊加等，悉議加封。

translations.literal: Thereupon Lao Zhang was made Grand Tutor, Toqan was made director of the Liaoyang Branch Privy Council, and Qutu Temür was still enfeoffed as Prince of Yangdi in succession; Princes Nangia and others were all considered for added enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Lao Zhang was made Grand Tutor, Toqan director of the Liaoyang Branch Privy Council, Qutu Temür enfeoffed as Prince of Yangdi, and Princes Nangia and others were all considered for enhanced titles.

sentences.zh: 尋又詔加封老章和寧王，以嶺北行省丞相知行樞密院事，俾鎮北藩云。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward an edict further enfeoffed Lao Zhang as Prince of Hening, with him as Liaobei Branch Secretariat chancellor acting as Privy Council director, ordering him to guard the northern frontier, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Lao Zhang was further enfeoffed as Prince of Hening, made Liaobei Branch Secretariat chancellor acting Privy Council director, and charged with guarding the northern frontier.
